document.title: Afghanistan: Taliban Leader Mullah Omar: Intimations of Radical Pan-Islamic Thinking?
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), 1998 Missile Strikes on Bin Laden May Have Backfired
document.note: [Secret] The Department questions its assumption that Mullah Omar has only Afghan nationalist goals. His statements suggest growing sympathy for pan-Islamic movements such as al-Qaeda, possibly through bin Laden's influence. Omar is described as poorly educated and unsure of foreign affairs, and the Taliban might never expel bin Laden. Excised.

key_claims: Omar's reported statements suggest a possible drift toward radical pan-Islamism, against prior view of him as a traditionalist Deobandi.
Many observers believe bin Ladin, in Kandahar since early 1997, is close to Omar and may influence him, despite Taliban 'guest' claims.
Bin Ladin has funded Taliban projects, which may add to his influence.
Unconfirmed reports said Omar married bin Ladin's daughter in August 1998; Taliban denied.
Taliban would possibly never expel bin Ladin because they see his cause as theirs.
Taliban might redirect forces to Kashmir, Central Asia, Uighurs in China, or Pakistan once consolidated.
The Saudi/Taliban split removes a moderating influence.
